title: Finite scalar restriction preserves constructible complexes and bounds
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $a:A\to A'$ a homomorphism of finite commutative rings, and $a_X:A_X\to A'_X$ the induced morphism of constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is exact on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and thus induces a termwise functor $D(a_X):D(A'_X)\to D(A_X)$ on unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It sends each constructible sheaf of $A'_X$-modules to a constructible sheaf of $A_X$-modules [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], using the same stratification and trivializing covers. For every $L\in D(A'_X)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, $H^q(D(a_X)L)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}H^q(L)$. In particular it preserves bounded constructibility and preserves and reflects vanishing of cohomology in each degree. Surjectivity of $a$ is not assumed.

source.place: Second paragraph, last sentence: regard the outer finite-coefficient terms as R_n-modules by scalar restriction.

proof.text: Put $F=\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$. By [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], $F$ is additive and changes neither the underlying abelian sheaf nor the underlying maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1) to $A_X$ and $A'_X$ on the same small site: kernels and cokernels in both module categories have the corresponding underlying abelian sheaves. The kernel action on a subsheaf and the cokernel action on a quotient are induced by the original action; composing either action with $a_X$ gives exactly its restricted action. Thus $F$ preserves kernels and cokernels and is exact. Also $F(M)=0$ if and only if $M=0$, since both zero conditions say that this same abelian sheaf is zero.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; kernel and cokernel constructions immediately preceding it.

proof.text: For a stratum immersion $i:Z\to X$, use [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] for both finite rings to identify $i^{-1}A_X=A_Z$ and $i^{-1}A'_X=A'_Z$. These identifications commute with $a$: on the generating constant sections both composites send $b\in A$ to the constant section $a(b)$, hence they agree by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and the constant-presheaf construction in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. By the module inverse-image construction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the action on $i^{-1}M$ is $i^{-1}\mu_M$. Consequently applying inverse image to the restricted action gives $i^{-1}(\mu_M\circ(a_X\times1))=i^{-1}\mu_M\circ(i^{-1}a_X\times1)$. This is the restricted action on the inverse image. Tensoring along either coefficient isomorphism merely transports this action ($m\otimes r\mapsto c^{-1}(r)m$, inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$), so this gives $i_A^*F(M)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z}(i_{A'}^*M)$. Restriction to a covering object of the localized site commutes with scalar restriction section by section.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module (apply inverse image to the action); Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules; constant sheaves in Tag 093I, section-constant.

proof.text: For every $A'$-module $P$, scalar restriction of its constant module sheaf is the constant sheaf of $\operatorname{Res}_aP$. Indeed [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] constructs this sheaf by sheafifying the constant module presheaf. By [lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification], for either coefficient ring its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification of that presheaf; these are the same abelian presheaf $P$. On locally represented constant sections the two $A$-actions are both $(b,p)\mapsto a(b)p$, so the identity of the abelian sheafifications is $A$-linear. If $M$ is constructible, choose its stratification and the covers trivializing each stratum as in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Apply the preceding step and this constant-model calculation to each chosen trivialization. They give trivializations of $F(M)$ on the very same strata and covering objects, with models $\operatorname{Res}_aP$.

source.place: Tag 093I, section-constant, and Tag 093Q, definition-locally-constant; the constant model with its induced scalar action.

proof.text: The stalks of the restricted sheaf on each stratum have the same underlying sets as the original stalks: the neighbourhood diagram and its equivalence relation in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] are unchanged, and the action on representatives is precomposed with $a$. Each original stalk is finitely generated over the finite ring $A'$, hence is finite as a set: if it has $t$ generators, it is a quotient of the finite set $(A')^t$. Its restricted $A$-module is therefore finitely generated by the finite list of all its elements (each element is $1$ times itself). Thus the unchanged stratification and trivializations from step 3 satisfy the finite-stalk condition of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] over $A$. This proves preservation of constructible sheaves. No surjectivity of $a$ was used.

source.place: Tag 09AJ, definition-constructible; apply its locally constant finite-type condition using the unchanged finite stalks.

proof.text: By step 1, $F$ satisfies the additive exactness hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply that node to the two module-sheaf categories on our small site, using a common localization universe: termwise $C(F)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces $D(a_X)$, with $D(a_X)(QK)\cong Q(C(F)K)$ for every unbounded complex $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^q(C(F)K)\cong F(H^q(K))$, naturally in $K$. The cohomology functors on the derived categories are the factorizations of complex cohomology through $Q$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The preceding natural comparison therefore gives $H^q(D(a_X)L)\cong F(H^q(L))$ for every $L$: for a representative $L=QK$ it is precisely that comparison on $K$, and naturality for a quasi-isomorphism remains commutative after inverting it, hence also for roofs in the localization. This uses no boundedness or resolution hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, especially (3)-(4); cohomology comparison from homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor.

proof.text: Combine step 5 with the zero-reflection observation of step 1. For every $q$, $H^q(D(a_X)L)=0$ if and only if $F(H^q(L))=0$, if and only if $H^q(L)=0$. Hence every vanishing bound is preserved and reflected. In particular, if the cohomology of $L$ vanishes outside $[r,s]$, the same is true after restriction; this is the boundedness condition in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. If all cohomology sheaves of $L$ are constructible, steps 3-4 and the isomorphism of step 5 show the same for $D(a_X)L$. Thus bounded constructibility is preserved, with the original interval $[r,s]$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q14-19dd255f2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS. This is the first split of a node Q34 created on 2026-10-21; there is no repair note, it is not on the dropped list, live and side-live still show it unsplit, and it adds no new nodes. The statement is unchanged; the added stmt_dep def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories is needed for 'bounded constructibility'. The statement is a true generalization of the source sentence in main-20261015 sk-prop-integral-criterion-reductions.proof.md, second paragraph, last sentence ('restriction of scalars, which preserves constructibility'): it allows any homomorphism of finite commutative rings, and the parent det-prop-integral-criterion-reductions step 4 uses it for the quotients Λ_n→Λ_{n-1} and Λ_n→Λ_1. Both coefficient rings are constant ring sheaves on the same small pro-étale site; no completed coefficients are mixed in. Steps: (1) exactness and zero reflection follow from def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars (same underlying abelian sheaf) and lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful(1). (2) I checked the square c_{A'}∘i^{-1}a_X = a_Z∘c_A on constant sections, using prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, which allows any morphism and the empty scheme; the two A_Z-actions on i^{-1}M agree because of this square. (3) For the constant models, lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification shows the underlying abelian sheafification does not depend on the ring, so Res of the constant sheaf of P is the constant sheaf of Res_a P. On the localized site the definition uses the restricted ring sheaf; this is harmless because the action is fixed by the local formula. (4) Res leaves the stalk sets unchanged; a finitely generated module over finite A' is finite, hence finitely generated over A, and the step does not assume A'-generators stay A-generators. (5) The Mathlib leaves mapDerivedCategoryFactors and homologyFunctorIso give the unbounded derived functor and the natural comparison H^q(Res L) ≅ Res H^q(L), with no resolution needed. (6) Vanishing is preserved and reflected, so bounded constructibility holds with the same interval [r,s]. Small cases checked: X empty, A'=0, the identity, Z/4→Z/2, and F_2→F_4 (non-surjective). Stacks tags checked against tags/tags: 03DA, 03D2, 03D3, 093I, 093Q, 09AJ, 015F (derived.tex:5884, unbounded clauses 3–4) and 010N. No SGA source is used. Candidates read and found not to be duplicates: lem-weil-pbc-constructible-change-of-ring (étale site, surjective map, two-way equivalence), lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact and def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars (completed coefficients), def-sfb-derived-restrict-levelwise, lem-pe-coefficient-constructible-iso and lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-constructibility-test. The declared tool uses lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful and prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map are generic and accepted. No fixes.
